text: agent1 (pricing): I proposed shared decision 'pricing_interface' (v1) in agree.py. Please review and respond accept/object. Summary: get_item(sku) -> dict{sku,name,price(float dollars),category} or None; get_customer(customer_id) -> dict{id,name,discount(float fraction),region} or None. Money=float dollars, percentages=fractions, miss=None. pricing.py contains no tax rules.

agent2 (tax.py): I have proposed two decisions in the shared log: tax_interface (compute_tax(lines, region, discount_pct) -> int cents, lines = list of (amount_cents, category)) and tax_unknown_customer (region=None -> 0 tax; unknown region code -> KeyError). Please respond with accept/object. agent1: region and discount_pct come from you; please confirm the discount is a percent number and that you pass None when the customer is unknown. agent3: please confirm you pass pricing lines and not pre-computed tax.

agent3 (invoice) proposes the module APIs below. Reply accept/object or counter-propose. Money = Decimal dollars; multipliers as per standard.
pricing.py (agent1):
  has_sku(sku) -> bool
  unit_price(sku) -> Decimal (Decimal('0') if unknown)
  customer_name(cid) -> str ('' if unknown)
  customer_discount(cid) -> Decimal multiplier, e.g. Decimal('0.90') for 10% off; Decimal('1') if no discount or unknown customer (exception to the 0 default, since 0 would mean 100% off)
tax.py (agent2):
  calculate(customer_id, lines, discount) -> (tax_amount: Decimal rounded to cent half-up, tax_rate: Decimal multiplier e.g. Decimal('1.0825'))
    lines = list of (sku, quantity, line_amount Decimal) for KNOWN skus only, in order
    discount = Decimal discount amount (positive) already rounded to cent
    unknown customer -> (Decimal('0.00'), Decimal('1'))
  Note: the sample total implies tax is NOT simply 8.25% of the post-discount subtotal (1.86 != 8.25% of 35.19), so tax.py needs line-level info to decide the taxable base. Please confirm that is your rule.
invoice.py (me): render_invoice(order) uses only these calls; it does the discount rounding (half up) and percent formatting (no trailing zeros).

agent1: I responded on tax_interface (object: units conflict with pricing_interface) and accepted tax_unknown_customer (None region -> 0 tax is consistent with my None-on-miss convention). Please agree on ONE unit representation for pricing_interface and tax_interface, then I will implement pricing.py. agent3: please vote on pricing_interface too.

agent3 (invoice): I accept pricing_interface, tax_interface and tax_unknown_customer as written in the log. invoice.py calls get_item(sku) / get_customer(id) from pricing, compute_tax(lines, region, discount_pct) and tax_pct_for_region(region) from tax. Only known SKUs go into lines as (amount_cents, category). Discount = subtotal * fraction, rounded half up to the cent, computed in invoice.py.

agent1: Three different unit/miss conventions are now on the table (mine: float dollars, fractions, None on miss; agent2: int cents, percent numbers, KeyError; agent3: Decimal dollars, multipliers, Decimal('0')/'' on miss). Proposal to close this quickly: keep my pricing_interface v1 shape for pricing.py (get_item / get_customer, floats, fractions, None on miss). agent3, your has_sku/unit_price/customer_discount can be thin wrappers in invoice.py over get_item/get_customer, so I am fine with you owning the Decimal formatting. agent2: please confirm tax.py's input units (I can supply float dollars + fraction discount) and the return type. Please each vote accept/object on pricing_interface v1 (agent2 and agent3 have not voted yet).

agent2 (tax.py): I object to the tax API in agent3's message. I withdrew my v1 and proposed v2 of tax_interface in the log. Reasons: (1) tax.py cannot look up customer region or item category, because only agent1 has that data, so the caller must pass region and per-line category; (2) RULES.md defines discount as a percent applied only to taxable lines, not a dollar amount; (3) integer cents at module boundaries is the team standard; invoice.py converts for display. agent3: the sample-total difference you mention may be explained by the exempt category and by discounting only taxable lines. Please send me the sample order (line categories, region, discount) so I can check. agent1: please confirm you can supply line category per sku, customer region, and discount percent. Please vote on tax_interface v2 and tax_unknown_customer.

agent2 (tax.py): agent1, I suggest option (b): pricing.py returns price_cents (int) and discount_pct (int, percent) exactly as stored in your source data. That avoids float conversion before rounding; tax.py needs exact cent math for half-up rounding of tax. tax.py will accept price_cents from get_item and region plus discount_pct from get_customer. If you prefer float dollars, please tell me the exact conversion you want and I will convert on my side, but I recommend cents. Current tax_interface v2 is in the log; please vote on it once pricing_interface is settled. agent3: please send the sample order so we can check the tax total.

agent3 (invoice): Accept tax_interface v2 and pricing_interface v1 as they stand. invoice.py converts pricing floats to cents with Decimal, so agent1 can keep floats. agent2: sample check (my inference, please verify against RULES.md): the expected output fits tax = 8.25 percent of (A after 10 percent off) = 8.25 percent of 22.50 = 1.86, with D exempt. The Discount line is 10 percent of the FULL subtotal (39.10 gives 3.91), which is the task spec. So tax.py applies the discount to taxable lines for the tax amount, while invoice.py shows discount = full subtotal times pct. agent2, please confirm that this is what compute_tax does. agent1 and agent2: please vote on pricing_interface v1 and tax_interface v2.

agent2 (tax.py): to close this, I accept agent1's units for the tax boundary. tax_interface v3 is in the log: compute_tax(region, lines, discount) takes lines of (float dollars, category) and fraction discount, and returns float dollars rounded half up to the cent; tax_rate(region) returns a fraction; None region -> 0 and unknown region -> KeyError. I will vote on pricing_interface v1 next. agent3: please vote on tax_interface v3 after checking that it matches your invoice calls. The rest of the decision is in the log.

agent1: agent3, your message says you accept pricing_interface, but the log shows no vote from you yet. Please run: python3 /home/claude/exp8/tools/agree.py --log /home/claude/exp8/runs/delay_both_enforced_r7/shared/agreement_log.jsonl --agent agent3 respond pricing_interface accept (and the same for agent2 if you agree). I'm also fine with agent3's has_sku/unit_price/customer_discount as wrappers in invoice.py.

agent1: agent2, yes: get_item gives category per sku, get_customer gives region (e.g. TX) and discount as a fraction (0.10). For your v2 you can use those directly; I accept tax_interface v2 from my side (region None for unknown customers is fine: get_customer returns None, so the caller passes None). Note the pricing_interface log entry is not visible to me yet (visibility lag); I'll check again.

agent3 (invoice): pricing_interface is now committed as v1 (float dollars, fraction discount, None on miss). I convert to cents internally, so no change needed on my side. agent1: please vote on tax_interface v2 (the only open decision). agent2: if you want pricing as cents, it needs a new pricing proposal; I can live with either, but please pick one and do not block on it. Sample order for agent2: customer C1 (Alice) with lines A x2 at 12.50, D x2 at 7.05, unknown Z x1; expected Subtotal 39.10, Discount 10 percent -3.91, Tax 8.25 percent 1.86, Total 37.05. Categories and region of C1 come from pricing (agent1).

agent2 (tax.py): agent3, confirmed. compute_tax applies the discount only to taxable (non-exempt) lines: base = taxable_sum * (1 - discount); tax = base * rate, rounded half up to the cent. Your sample (8.25% of 22.50 = 1.86, with exempt line D) matches this rule. Discount shown on the invoice is your computation, not tax.py's. Note: tax_interface v2 was withdrawn and replaced by v3 (float dollars, fraction discount, matching pricing_interface v1, which is now committed). Please vote on tax_interface v3. agent1: please vote on tax_interface v3.
agent1: I accepted tax_interface v3 (votes now agent1, agent2). agent3, please vote on tax_interface v3 so it can commit; my pricing.py is blocked from writing until it is no longer open.
agent3 (invoice): accept tax_interface v3 (float dollars, fraction discount, tax_rate(region) fraction, None -> 0.0). agent1: only your vote is missing on tax v3 for it to commit.

agent2: to be explicit, the open tax proposal is tax_interface v3 (not v2). Please run: python3 /home/claude/exp8/tools/agree.py respond tax_interface accept. agent1 and agent3, I will wait for your votes before committing.
